name: Per-character blur reveal

source.description: 1 inspected reference film (batch-3, 2026-11-26): a silent milestone film writes its closing thank-you line letter by letter from blur to sharp.

technique: Each letter of a short line appears in turn, from heavy blur and low opacity to sharp, so a quiet or grateful line arrives softly instead of popping. The left-to-right stagger reads like the line being breathed out.
purpose: Let a quiet or grateful line arrive softly instead of popping; the stagger reads like the line being breathed out.
visual_behaviour: Each letter of a short line appears in turn, from heavy blur and transparency to sharp, left to right, in about a second.
mechanics: Split into characters; per character, filter blur 12-16 px -> 0 and opacity 0 -> 1 over about 0.3 s (power2.out), stagger 0.07 s; a 10-character line completes in about 1.1 s (ref-cfaf668ebf 42.47-43.53 s, 15 fps strip). Optional colour gradient across the line. Final glyph positions stay fixed (no tracking change).

decomposition.timing: 0.07 s stagger, about 0.3 s per character, about 1 s per short line; hold at least 1.5 s.

use_cases: A closing thank-you or emotional line
A quiet section opener after a dip
A word that should feel soft rather than stamped
failure_modes: Blur on many large letters costs filter time every frame; cap at about 20 characters
A long stagger on a long line drags; switch to per-word

implementation.approach: Studio.type.split into characters; per character a CSS blur 12-16 px to 0 with opacity 0 to 1 over about 0.3 s (power2.out), stagger 0.07 s; glyph positions fixed. Cap at about 20 characters (blur filters cost raster time); switch to per-word for longer lines.

provenance.observed: A thank-you line appears letter by letter, each letter going from blurred and transparent to sharp, about 0.07 s apart, in 1.1 s.

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown).
